references.text: The Valley of Achor is mentioned here as the place where Achan was stoned, which explains the origin of the name (Achor means 'trouble')
En-shemesh and En-rogel are also mentioned in the description of Benjamin's border, showing that these places marked the boundary between Judah and Benjamin
Debir is mentioned earlier in this chapter as a city that was captured, and may be related to the place name in the border description
Gilgal was the place where the Israelites first camped after crossing the Jordan, and served as an important reference point in the border description
En-rogel is mentioned as the place where Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited to bring messages to David
En-rogel is mentioned in connection with Adonijah's attempt to make himself king
The prophet Hosea mentions the Valley of Achor as a future place of hope, which gives theological depth to the geographical reference
